summary: A colour, radius, shadow or font written past the theme where the theme has a token for it; each finding names the token to use.
Spacing (a margin, padding or gap) off the theme's spacing scale; each finding names the step to use.
A card or row that is one link where a click at some spot on it opens nothing, as when the page positions a part of it and the link's layer stops there.
A card whose hover or keyboard focus reveals a part and moves the card's own box or anything around it.
The pane a person looks at (the open modal dialog, else the main landmark) draws nothing to read, nothing to press and no named progress.
A modal dialog a person can put away over a page that would strand them: blank behind it, or signed out with no way to sign in.
A page marked signed out (data-ouro-session) that shows the empty state a signed-in person would see, such as All caught up.
Running text drawn too large to read: the size most of a page's running text is drawn at is over 24px, as when an app grows its root type with the screen.
A page with stylesheets and no fragmentFocusScript after them, where Safari takes focus as later stylesheets load on the page opened at a place on it.
Prose that wraps at a reading measure well under the column it sits in, held by a max-width; the fix is to let text use its column, or declare the measure in ouro-check.json.

A popup drawn, on a frame after it opens, somewhere other than where it settles, as one measured against the viewport and drawn inside a layer further down the page is; the fix is to place it where it settles from its first frame (position: fixed).

In an engine without corner-shape (an app's WKWebView), a drawn surface rounded under half its size by a plain circular radius, not clipped to a squircle; the fix is to add squircleCorners() to the build's PostCSS plugins, or clip the surface to a squircle with clip-path. Run it with --engine webkit.
Two dividing lines side by side where one would separate, such as a list's last row's border against its card's; each finding names both elements.

widened: a lighter framed surface inside a frame at any inset, including when clipped
summary: Remove the inner border and use a step between theme surface tokens.
A count badge on an icon that is clipped by a box around it, whose numerals sit off its middle, or that sits at another offset from its icon than the page's other badges.
A pointer cursor on an element that is no control and holds none: a person expects a press to do something, and a keyboard can't reach it.
Two separate surfaces, or a surface and the edge of the one it sits in, that are neither touching nor at least the minimum gap (--ouro-gap-min) apart.
A box that moves in a transition but whose edge, in one frame at 60 fps, moves half its travel or more; the fix is to ease the whole move on one easing and duration. Run in Chromium or WebKit.
A box that goes back before it arrives in a transition, by more than 10% of its travel; the fix is to move each edge one way to where it ends.
A box next to a moving one that changes place or size on the frames of its transition; the fix is to animate transform or opacity and leave the neighbours' layout alone.
Text that wraps to a different number of lines while a transition runs; the fix is to hold the text's width through the move.
A text, or a box over 100 square pixels, that goes from invisible to visible, or back, in one frame inside a transition; the fix is to fade or grow it on the transition that moves its box.
A box whose edge passes where it ends by more than 2 pixels in a transition, as a max-width that animates to a cap does; the fix is to animate transform.
A box with a two-keyframe transition whose edge strays more than 2 pixels from its own easing curve, as one a script or observer resizes every frame does; the fix is to let the transition move it.
A box or text whose opacity changes more than 0.1 beyond its own easing in one frame of a transition; the fix is to fade it over the whole transition.
Text cut off by its own clipping box mid-transition that fits at the end; the fix is to size the box to the text or reveal both together.
A press after which one frame took over 50 ms (the jank rule's budget is 250 ms); the fix is to keep the handler to a few milliseconds.

One line of words in a control (a button, a field's value or placeholder, an editor, or a bare text area inside its frame) whose cap height sits off the control's middle, as a composer's placeholder pushed low by a bottom-aligned row does.
A control holding an icon, a picture or a typed glyph such as "…" whose ink sits more than 1px off the control's middle, across or down, as a typed "…" on its text baseline does.

An open panel that isn't modal (a menu, a popover, or a data-ouro-panel) 120px or taller where under 60% of its inside has text, a control or a picture within 24px, as a wide panel with its links in one narrow column is.
In an open panel, words of 60 characters or fewer that wrap on a screen 1024px wide or wider (24 below it), as a one-line description in a narrow column does.
In an open panel, a rounded box with a fill or a border on every side that holds words and nothing to press: a decorative card in a menu.
An open panel whose bottom passes the bottom of the screen with nothing to scroll it into view; the fix is to cap its height and let its inside scroll.
In a panel a press opens, words cut off by the box around them that hides its overflow; an ellipsis, a line clamp and a folded box pass.
